methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $6M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Albacore is a seed-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by John Huddleston and Dante Vaisbort. The company has raised $6.5M to date. The valuation universe consists of three private peers in the ocean and maritime sector (Standard Subsea, Clippership, and NetworkOcean); no public comparables exist in this space.

Given the limited methodological toolkit available for an early-stage company with sparse public market data, stage-progression analysis was applied. Using total capital raised ($6.5M) as a proxy for current value and applying a standard seed-to-Series A step-up multiplier of 2.5x, this method implies a valuation of $16M. This represents the sole quantitative approach available given the data constraints.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $14M (low) to $19M (high), with a median implied value of $16M. The narrow range reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than convergence across multiple independent approaches. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific subsector, the quality of financial and operational data underlying private peer selection, and whether the comparable set adequately reflects Albacore's market position and technical differentiation. A more robust valuation would benefit from revenue multiples or venture capital method analysis once additional financial metrics are available.
